reviews.text: Our training sessions with Janet have really made a difference. Our communication skills with Scorpio have improved and his demeanor is much calmer.

We initially started with Opportunity Barks for their training assistance with our very young and rambunctious Cocker Spaniel at both their East Falls location and farm. Within very little time our puppy made strides in both social behavior and paying attention to us while out and about. We are extremely happy to continue using their farm camp program frequently as an outlet for our dog to have play days. Reuben is always thrilled to see Laura at the morning pick ups in East Falls which is very convenient for our work schedule.Rachel is always easy to reach for scheduling and any other questions.

We recently completed the Puppy Foundations course with Janet and John and it was a great experience for our pup as well as
for my wife and me.

We first met Janet and John through attending the puppy socials and we were struck by how well they managed the group of chaotic little puppies to create a positive play experience - both Janet and John made sure each dog was feeling safe, secure and having a blast by being very attentive and always created space or added activities depending on the needs of the group. In addition to being a great time for all of the pups, during these socials Janet and John made themselves resources to the group by checking in on our training progress and talking through concerns and questions that we were facing. Having such a positive experience in the socials made it an easy decision to pursue the Puppy Foundations course with our little buddy.

The training space is large and always very clean and orderly, with a bed, toys and separate space for each pup and their parents. The training curriculum feels very intentional and is structured to build on itself week-to-week, going from name recognition to practicing leash walking over the course of 4 weeks. During classes Janet and John were engaged with each family to identify individual needs, habits and discuss to any concerns. I never left class feeling like we failed and each week we learned learned a little more than the last.

Overall our experience with Opportunity Barks for puppy socials and the Puppy Foundations course was extremely positive.  Janet and John are both excellent trainers and I would recommend them and Opportunity Barks to anyone with a new pup and/or seeking training.

My dog, Shiro, and I are a couple of OpBarks stans! I first brought Shiro for training when he was 8 mos old, and our love affair with this team is still going strong 9 years later. Farm Dog day is Shiro's favorite day of the week...He gets so excited when we pull up to the van and see Laura, hopping right in! I love the staff-to-dog ratio and that Farm Dog combines training with fun - running the trails, splashing in the creek, chasing the ATV - and socialization. Shiro underwent emergency IVDD surgery Nov 2024, and Rachel amazingly checked in at regular intervals to see how he was healing. OpBarks is truly invested in the wellbeing of your pup and treats you like family! Thankfully, Shiro made a full recovery, and returning to Farm Dog has really helped strengthen his hind legs. We are lifelong devotees! Plus, they take the BEST pictures of my handsome guy. 🥰

Archie has been attending Opbarks for nearly three years, and I truly cannot imagine our week without it. That one day of running, splashing in the creek, and just being a dog has made such a visible difference. He has grown so much in his comfort with other dogs, his listening, and his ability to thrive in high-stimulation environments. As the owner of a pretty anxious pup, the thing that matters most to me is trust, and the team has earned it completely. They are always communicative, accommodating, and no matter what, Archie is happy to get on that bus every single time. He also gets his nails trimmed weekly during his farm camp session, which doubles as handling training, a huge bonus. He comes home exhausted and happy, and we could not ask for more. Archie and I are lifers.
Pip loves op barks day care. He comes home tired and happy. I’ve also worked with op barks for training. Pip wouldn’t be the dog he is today without the support provided and his friends at op barks!

Opportunity Barks was a lifesaver for training my German shepherd (we did the board and train). I continue sending him to the Op Barks Farm Dog program 1-2x per week so he can play with dogs in a safe environment and go on adventures (hiking, creek, supervised playtime). It’s an amazing program and the team is absolutely wonderful (shoutout to Laura!). We also use Op Barks for boarding when we’re out of town. Couldn’t speak more highly of it!

Opportunity Barks Really knows what they are doing in the dog Training Dept .They also took the time to train me on ways to better help my puppy.My puppy is going to The Farm off leash program and he loves it . I also really like the  daily feed back I get  when he returns in the form of videos and reports.My trainers are Britt and Alyssa they are really great. and clearly love their jobs and dogs .Looking forward to doing more training with them and my dog Remi .

Hey Katie, Thanks for coming to hang and bringing Branson to the puppy social. He’s a really thoughtful, observant pup, and you’re doing a nice job letting him take things in while still guiding him toward engagement. Puppy socialization is about helping lil tater tots learn how to regulate, recover, and interact safely with the world, and Branson is right in that learning phase.

We’re really glad you came, and we’d love to see you both back at puppy social again soon- 
All of us at OpBarks

We used Leigh for 1:1 training classes for our spicy rescue puppy and she was a GOD SEND. Literally worth every penny. I thought I adopted a dog but the first weeks she was more like an alligator and we were in over our head! Leigh has an amazing ability to read dog behavior as she simultaneously interviews the handlers to find out about their goals and lifestyle. She doesn’t just teach commands but actually gave us a COMMUNICATION line with our dog. The lessons learned are easy to apply to other areas of the dogs life and she is always giving ideas how to take things further in the future when the pup is ready. Over ~ 6 weeks of consistent training our dog stopped biting, was able to find calm during her day, and showed that she TRUSTED US. Honestly it was the best money we could have spent on our pup. We get compliments at family events and from strangers about how well behaved our girl is now. My advice: book the classes, do your homework, and love your dog!!
Thank you Leigh 🙏🏻🙏🏻

I had a terrible experience with Opportunity Barks. The City School program keeps the dogs crated for 6 of the 7 hours they are there.  The 1 hour of training includes potty breaks. When I picked up my 8 month old puppy she was so desperate to pee and poo, she went on the sidewalk in front of their building.  She was so thirsty she was panting and needed water immediately.  I sent food but she did not eat there.

To compound the problem, Communication is awful.  They don't let you into the space.  You stand on the sidewalk - they crack open the door and pull her in or give you the leash to take her out.  You get 1 email a week with some photos and videos. They don't appear to read the form you fill out and don't discuss goals.  I told them that my puppy has had training since birth, but their first video was showing me how to hold a leash.  The second video was of a different dog being trained - they said my dog was tethered watching.  Throughout the entire video I could hear her crying.  No one attempted to soothe her at all. I provided constructive input verbally and in writing by email.

Despite my bad experience at the City School, I was still interested in the Farm School.  I went to the open house and they were much more transparent about what a typical day looks like there.  But before the evaluation day (which is separate from the City School evaluation), they called me to say that they were cancelling the evaluation because I am not a good fit for their program.  They said it had nothing to do with my dog, who is a very sweet Labrador,  it is because I am not "aligned" with them.  They were not willing to even listen to why I thought the Farm School would be a better fit than the City School, saying that the decision had been made "by senior management" and it is not worth wasting time talking about it.  Wow!

We had previously trusted Opportunity Barks with our 2-year-old dog, but our most recent 10-day stay was extremely disappointing. The manager at the boarding and training facility has changed in the past year, and unfortunately, our experience under the new management was far below the standards we had previously expected.

When we picked him up, he had diarrhea and arrived with a soiled behind — yet we were never notified of any stomach issues during his stay. He also had a deep scratch across his nose, which we only noticed in the daily photos and had to point out to staff ourselves in order to get him proper care. When we submitted a review after his stay, staff claimed they had informed us about the scratch and that he hadn’t had any stomach issues while in their care. Diarrhea is very evident with our white Samoyed, as his fur gets soiled and requires extra cleaning, so their claims felt like gaslighting rather than honest communication.

Instead of acknowledging their mistakes or committing to improve, staff told us we were no longer welcome and even blocked our portal login. Their response was dismissive, unprofessional, and demonstrated a complete lack of accountability.

For the health and safety of your dog, stay away from Opportunity Barks and their unethical, unprofessional behavior.
